candidates.hypothesis: Maker-side fade of the 3rd-Friday SOQ spike: resting sell limit k ticks above the Friday 08:30 CT open, trade-through fill, cover by 11:00 CT
candidates.mechanism: SOQ-related buying pressure into the Friday open that reverses by noon ET (Baltussen-Terstegge-Whelan, owner RD4)
candidates.published_effect: ES futures reversal -12.89 bp (t -2.40, sd 80.45) after +14.30 bp into the open
candidates.dispersion: t -2.40, sd 80.45 bp (as quoted by RD4)
candidates.quote: The average overnight cumulative return in the active futures contract is equal to 14 bps which completely reverses by 12:00.
candidates.quote_location: RD4 evidence row (R17 did not re-read the paper)
candidates.why: Limit-entry variant of RD4-C1's short leg; the limit saves ~0.5 tick on a ~31-tick move but at trade-through fills it fills only if price keeps rising after 08:30 (adverse selection within the event)

candidates.overlap_note: same mechanism as RD4-C1/R12; differs only by resting limit entry instead of market order; lead merges

candidates.hypothesis: Expiry-day pinning: on serial ES-options expiry Fridays, rest limits fading moves away from the nearest 5-pt strike in the last 30 min, flat by 15:05 CT
candidates.mechanism: market makers' delta-hedge rebalancing pulls futures to the ATM strike (Golez-Jackwerth 2012)
candidates.best_source: Golez, Jackwerth (2012) Pinning in the S&P 500 futures, JFE 106(3) 566-585
candidates.published_effect: abs-return distribution shift of at least 11.00 bp Thu PM to Fri PM; $59M of $115M notional shift in last 30 min
candidates.price_level_used: ES 6000 (11 bp = 6.6 ES pt; NOT a per-trade P&L)
candidates.quote: We find in the long sample (November 1992 until November 2009) a shift of at least 11.00 bps from Thursday PM to expiration Friday PM. ... An amazing $59 million shifts solely within the last 30 min of trading.
candidates.decay_evidence: none read; ES options OI has migrated to weeklies/0DTE since sample
candidates.data_needed: 1-min bars, serial-expiry calendar, strike grid; OI by strike for conditioning
candidates.data_cost: options OI not owned; price not gathered
candidates.why: Published mechanism and timing in the last 30 min, but no trading rule or per-trade gross; old sample; ~8 events/yr
candidates.prop_notes: intraday, flat by 15:05 CT; few orders; not HFT
candidates.overlap_note: no pinning member in the index; not covered by RD5/R1 (grep)

candidates.hypothesis: Provide liquidity against the preannounced commodity ETF/GSCI roll in CL calendar spread; hold until spread narrows
candidates.mechanism: predictable roll flow widens second-front spread before/during the roll, reverses after (Bessembinder et al. 2016; Mou 2011)
candidates.entry_window_ct: roll days (USO 4-day roll; GSCI 5th-9th business day)
candidates.best_source: Bessembinder, Carrion, Tuttle, Venkataraman (draft June 2015; JFE 121(1) 2016)
candidates.published_effect: spread widens 25 bp per roll, narrows 26 bp per roll after
candidates.price_level_used: CL $70: 25 bp = $0.175/bbl = 17.5 ticks on the spread
candidates.quote: widening of the calendar spread between the second- and the front month contract prices in the days before and during the USO roll, which averages 25 basis points per roll.
candidates.decay_evidence: paper finds more liquidity providers on roll days and narrower spreads; likely competed away
